text:
maya: Heads up — scheduling a preflight for APAC-west edge cohort maintenance. NIC firmware + targeted GPU microcode roll, window: Tue 02:00-04:00 local (2026-04-07 02:00-04:00). Low traffic but want to be safe.
sam: ETA on node count impacted? need to know capacity delta for reserved tenants.
maya: ~180 nodes across two racks. Expected transient capacity hit ~18% if we cordon whole cohort for rolling reboots.
andre: Can we stagger by pool so burst capacity remains for jobs? prefer cohort-by-cohort rather than rack-by-rack.
jia: Agree. Suggest 3 cohorts: cohort-a (canary 12 nodes), cohort-b (80), cohort-c (88). Canary first, validate KV cache regen, then continue.
frank: Ops cost question — if we push canary and then backfill from burst pools, we'll incur spot-backfill spend. Ballpark extra $600/hr during backfill window.
lucy: Noted — I’ll loop in finance for post-mortem cost tagging.
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance: APAC-west NIC/GPU firmware — 2026-04-07 02:00-04:00 local. Reminder 30m before.
maya: runbook highlights:
maya: - canary cohort first, run health checks, verify p95 latency and egress QPS
maya: - if latency > 1.5x baseline or error rate > 0.5%, abort and rollback
maya: - warm KV cache seed after reboot to avoid cold-cache latency spikes
sam: Add checkpoint: update routing policy to prefer eu-west fallback for critical customer routes during cohort-b. TTL 10m for route switch.
jia: For warm seeding use this command (will run after canary warmup):
jia: ```
jia: ./kvseed --cohort=cohort-a --parallel=6 --rate=5000
jia: ```
andre: Drain command we'll use (k8s evict wrapper):
andre: ```
andre: ./drain-node --node $NODE --grace-period 120 --eviction-rate 5
andre: ```
frank: Who owns CS comms to dedicated customers? we need to mention possible short throttles and canary timeframe.
lucy: I'll draft a short note and send to @cs-eng for review. deliverable by EOD.
maya: Monitoring checks (to be done by oncall):
maya: - pre: baseline perf snapshot (lat/errs/cpu/gpu-temp/egress)
maya: - post-canary: compare KV hitrate, p95, tail qps
maya: - continuous: model-serving error spikes, missing actor heartbeats
sam: Also throttle policy: lower non-critical batch qos to avoid starved latency path. Set batch cap from 128->64 for the window.
jia: We need to ensure autoscaler config won't aggressively scale GPU pools into the maintenance cohort. Patch applied:
jia: ```yaml
jia: autoscaler:
jia:   cooldown: 300
jia:   avoid_pools: ["apac-west-cohort-a","apac-west-cohort-b"]
jia: ```
andre: Canary rollout plan:
andre: - 02:00 canary (12 nodes) drain + reboot + smoke tests (30m)
andre: - 02:40 if green -> cohort-b (80 nodes) staggered over 40m
andre: - 03:40 cohort-c (88 nodes) finish by 04:20 if no issues
frank: If anything goes funky, abort and failover routing to eu-west. Who flips that? sam?
sam: I'll flip route and monitor for errors. Have rollback runbook ready.
maya: CS note flag: Dedicated clients on reserved capacity may see slight increase in latency for short windows; no scheduled downtime.
lucy: Draft done, sending now.
ops-bot: Deployment note: autoscaler patch merged to canary cluster 01:14 UTC.
andre: After reboot, run KV prefetch and prefix-cache seeding to reduce token cost spikes — reduces tokens served by ~8% in previous run.
jia: Also ensure node GPU thermals are tracked — set alert thresholds: GPU temp > 82C for >2m -> auto-cordon.
frank: Cost mitigation: prefer local burst backfill instead of cross-region failover to reduce egress costs. Decision: local first, fallback to eu-west only on failure.
maya: Final ask: team oncall please be around 01:45-04:30 local for quick actions. I'll post canary results in this thread.
sam: Acknowledged.
jia: Acknowledged.
andre: Acknowledged.
frank: Acknowledged.
lucy: Acknowledged.
ops-bot: Reminder 30m before: APAC-west maintenance (canary first)."
